analyticalMisses.summary: Cardinals Game 1 illustrates expression risk: STL ML at 51 cents won while STL over 4.5 team runs at 53 cents lost. Combined rounded risk $48, combined user-facing P/L -$10.09 net. The side handicap was directionally correct, but the larger team-total position required a much more specific offensive outcome. Future manuals should be cautious about over-weighting 'weak starter + taxed bullpen' into aggressive team-total sizing when a cheap side is also available.

NYM over 3.5 runs at 56 cents lost. The wager was selected as a cleaner offensive expression than the full-game side, but the offense did not deliver. Marked as a failed thesis/outcome -- not automatically proof of a process flaw. CLV is unavailable for this ticker (no valid pre-first-pitch archived observation exists), so a CLV-based read on selection quality cannot be completed for this bet.
Atlanta ML at 56 cents lost. One of the lower-conviction wagers on the final card, appropriately sized smaller at $10 rounded risk. Do not overreact to one result.

analyticalWins.summary: Best-expression success -- CWS team total. The manual initially considered the White Sox moneyline side but correctly upgraded the expression to CWS over 3.5 runs / 4+ runs around 50 cents, isolating the favorable offensive matchup without requiring Chicago's pitching/defense to produce a game win. Won, +$18.64 -- the largest individual profit in the batch.

Kansas City thesis succeeded across two correlated expressions: KC over 4.5 runs at 53 cents and KC F5 winner (three-way contract) at 55 cents both won. Combined rounded risk $28, combined user-facing profit +$22.50. Common thesis: attacking Oakland starter Mason Barnett early. Recorded as correlated / shared-thesis exposure, not two independent pieces of evidence.
Detroit ML at 50 cents won -- a strong price-sensitive side. The handicap preferred Detroit's starting-pitcher quality/length and viewed a pick'em price as favorable. User-facing profit +$13.05.

Price discipline remained valuable across the slate: several successful positions were bought around 50-55 cents rather than laying large favorite prices. The decision to pass expensive Dodgers F5 / Sugano-under pricing (no bet placed) should remain classified as a disciplined pass, not something to retroactively judge solely by the game result.

gameLevelConcentration.note: Correlated / shared-thesis exposure (attacking OAK starter Mason Barnett early), not two independent validations.
Correlated exposure: STL ML thesis was directionally correct (won), but the larger STL team-total position required a much more specific offensive outcome and lost.

processErrors.summary: Correlation discipline remains important. The two KC wagers won together but their outcomes were positively correlated -- do not count the 2-0 KC cluster as two fully independent validations. Conversely, the two STL Game 1 wagers demonstrate how correlated exposure can magnify a partially wrong expression even when the underlying side wins.

accountingConvention.description: Each individual screenshot Initial Cost is rounded UP (ceiling) to the nearest whole dollar to produce the user-facing true-cost/stake figure used for import stake and ROI accounting. Raw screenshot Initial Costs summed to $135.73; the rounded convention produces $138.00. The screenshot's exact Paid Out amount is preserved separately and verbatim on each bet's shareCardEvidence.shareCardPaidOut and confirmedReceiptReturn -- never rounded. Kalshi production fee economics (contractCost/entryFees/exitFees/executionEconomics fields) remain untouched by this user-facing rounding convention.
